answer: No. Frontmatter `authors:` credits only the page as a whole and does not cascade down to unsigned blocks, so an `@mention` elsewhere on the page without its own `-- @name` signature stays unattributed.

Memory for: If a page lists authors in its frontmatter, are @mentions further down the page credited to them?
[1] Authorship.md (The `-- @name` notation)
  `authors:` frontmatter: Declaring `authors:` in a page’s frontmatter credits the whole page, the same way `recipients:` addresses the whole page: / ```yaml / --- / authors: ["jo", "sam"] / --- / ``` / A wiki-link value in `authors:`, like `[[Jo]]`, is not a name and is silently ignored — unlike `recipients:`, which keeps a wiki link as an ordinary page link. / This does **not** cascade down to unsigned blocks in the page body: an `@mention` written elsewhere on the page without its own `-- @name` stays unattributed. Frontmatter `authors:` is page-level credit only — crediting a specific block still needs an inline signature on that block.
  - Declaring `authors: ["jo", "sam"]` in a page's frontmatter credits the whole page, the same way `recipients:` addresses the whole page.
  - Frontmatter `authors:` does not cascade down to unsigned blocks in the page body, so an @mention without its own `-- @name` stays unattributed.
  - Crediting a specific block requires an inline signature on that block, because frontmatter `authors:` gives page-level credit only.
[2] Tag/relation.md (relation)
  Kinds: * `mention`: a plain wikilink or markdown link (to a page, file, anchor, or external URL — see `toTag`). / * `at-mention`: an [[At-Mention|`@name` mention]] of an [[Identity]]. `to` is always the name’s `@name` identifier (`toTag: "identity"`). An identity is a name, so there is never a page behind it. / * `authored`: a block-ending signature or an `authors:` frontmatter declaration credits an identity. Signatures carry a source `range`. Page-level declarations do not. / * `co-mention`: two refs co-occurring in the same item (with its nested children) or paragraph. Emitted in both directions and dedup’d at the innermost shared scope. / * *user predicates*: any other `kind` value is a typed attribute edge whose label is the key (e.g. `spouse`). `from`/`fromTag` indicate whether it came from frontmatter, an inline attribute, or a data block.
[3] Guide/Comments, Mentions and Replies.md (Add a comment)
  - The authors: frontmatter field credits the page without attributing unsigned body text.
[4] Reference/Indexing Internals.md (Indexing process)
  Indexing process: [[Authorship|Signatures]] add a second relation kind alongside `at-mention`: `authored`. A block-ending `-- @name` signature emits one `authored` edge per name it credits, carrying a `range` into the signature text. An `authors:` frontmatter declaration emits the same kind with no `range`, crediting the whole page — the same shape a declared `recipients:` entry has. A signature also stamps `by` — the identity ids it credits — onto every `at-mention` relation inside the block it claims, so a query can join “who wrote this” onto “who it was addressed to” without a second pass.
  - An authors: frontmatter declaration emits an authored edge with no range, crediting the whole page.
Exact facts:
- [1] An **author** is an [[Identity]] you credit. A signature is an [[At-Mention]] used the other way around: an `@mention` **addresses** someone, while a signature **credits** someone. The same identities serve both — anyone you can mention, you can also sign as, including yourself.
